title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is computing 'motivic' invariants of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν} and of their compactifications. He works in a Grothendieck group K_!(S) with rational coefficients. In this group a Deligne–Mumford stack is assigned the class Σ_strata [coarse stratum]/|Aut|: stratify by automorphism group over geometric points and weight each stratum by 1/|Aut|. T(1) = [E^1] is the Tate class L. Specialising T(1) → 1 gives the orbifold Euler characteristic χ_!.

Where the page starts: the previous page gives a morphism over Z[1/2], M_{1,1} → [M_{0,4}/S_3] (Legendre λ-line modulo S_3). Over Z[1/2] it is a gerbe with constant band {±1}, since M_{1,1} = [M(2)/GL_2(F_2)] and M(2) → M_{0,4} is a μ_2-gerbe. Hence [M_{1,1}] = ½[M_{0,4}/S_3]. The coarse space of [M_{0,4}/S_3] is the j-line A^1. The generic stratum A^1 minus 2 points has weight 1; the orbit with stabilizer Z/2 (λ = -1, 2, 1/2) gives ½; the orbit with stabilizer Z/3 gives ⅓. So [M_{0,4}/S_3] = T − 2 + 5/6.

Formula (79): this yields [M_{1,1}] = ½(T(1) − 1) − 1/12 over Z[1/2] (more precisely Z[1/6]). The boundary M̂^∞_{1,1} is one point, the nodal cubic, whose automorphism group fixing the marked point is ±1. So it has class ½, and [M̂_{1,1}] = ½(T(1) − 1) + 5/12. Setting T = 1 gives χ(M_{1,1}) = −1/12 = ζ(−1) (Harer–Zagier) and χ(M̄_{1,1}) = 5/12, both correct.

Second computation over Spec Z: use the coarse map M_{1,1} → E^1 (the j-line). Two sections are singled out:
- S_0: j = 1728, Aut Z/4, weight ¼;
- S_1: j = 0, Aut Z/6, weight 1/6.
The two sections meet in the closed points a_2 (characteristic 2, j = 0 = 1728, Aut of order 24) and a_3 (characteristic 3, Aut of order 12). This gives the partition E^1 = U ⊔ S_0' ⊔ S_1' ⊔ {a_2} ⊔ {a_3}, with weights ½, ¼, 1/6, 1/24, 1/12.

The next page finishes the computation:
- [U] = T − 2 + ζ_2 + ζ_3, where ζ_p = [Spec F_p];
- [S_i'] = 1 − ζ_2 − ζ_3;
- result (80): [M_{1,1}] = ½(T − 1) − 1/12 + ⅛ζ_2 + ⅙ζ_3.
Check of the coefficients: ζ_2 gets ½ − 5/12 + 1/24 = 1/8 and ζ_3 gets ½ − 5/12 + 1/12 = 1/6, both correct. So (79) holds after inverting 6, and the ζ_p terms are the 'bad characteristic' corrections over Spec Z.
errors: (79) is stated 'au moins au dessus de Z[1/2]', but by the second computation it is exact only over Z[1/6]. Over Z[1/2] an extra term (1/6)ζ_3 appears from the characteristic-3 supersingular point. Grothendieck's own marginal note on the previous page ('valables au dessus de Z[1/6]') acknowledges this.
The transcription of the next page writes the weight of S'_1 as 7/6; it must be 1/6 (Aut Z/6), as the overbrace 1/4 + 1/6 = 5/12 confirms.
The struck-out '+T(1)+' in the second line of (79) should be ignored; the correct value is ½(T(1) − 1) + 5/12.

Caveat, not an error: this 1/|Aut|-weighted class is not Ekedahl's class of the stack (where [M_{1,1}] = L) and not the arithmetic groupoid count (#M_{1,1}(F_q) = q). It is a geometric 'coarse/inertia-weighted' invariant, and the notes do not make this distinction explicit.

ideas.what: Rational Grothendieck group in which a DM stack has class Σ [coarse stratum]/|Aut|, specialising to the orbifold Euler characteristic
ideas.modern_name: orbifold/stringy-type motivic class; constructible-function pushforward of 1/|Aut| into K_0(Var)⊗Q
ideas.usually_credited_to: Orbifold Euler characteristic: Harer–Zagier (1986), Thurston. Grothendieck ring of stacks: Ekedahl (2009), Behrend–Dhillon (2007), in a different normalisation.

ideas.modern_name: orbifold Euler characteristic of M_{1,1} and M̄_{1,1}, refined to a motivic class

ideas.what: Arithmetic refinement over Spec Z with correction terms ζ_p = [Spec F_p] = i_{p!}(1) coming from the characteristic-2 and characteristic-3 points with Aut of order 24 and 12
ideas.modern_name: class in K_0(Var_Z)⊗Q of the stack with bad-prime corrections
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; arithmetic of the j-line in characteristics 2 and 3 is classical (Deuring); Grothendieck rings over Z were studied later

ideas.what: Over Z[1/2], M_{1,1} is a μ_2-gerbe over [M_{0,4}/S_3] (Legendre form)

missed.claim: An explicit 1/|Aut|-weighted motivic class of M_{1,1} over Spec Z, including the exact bad-prime corrections ⅛ζ_2 + ⅙ζ_3. It shows that the naive formula valid over Z[1/6] fails over Z and quantifies the failure.
missed.quote: qui se rencontrent aux points 2 et 3, qui correspondent ... à des groupes d'automorphismes d'ordre 24, et 12
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This normalisation (distinct from Ekedahl's stack classes and from groupoid point counts) is a 'motivic orbifold Euler characteristic' over Spec Z. It is seldom computed with explicit corrections at small primes, and it predates Ekedahl and Behrend–Dhillon by decades.

missed.claim: The programme of computing such weighted classes for all M_{g,ν} and their compactifications over Spec Z, and of tracking the ζ_p corrections at primes p dividing automorphism orders, is only begun here (g = 0, ν = 4 and g = 1, ν = 1).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Weighted classes of this kind, as polynomials in L with corrections at small primes, are not systematically available in the literature, to my knowledge.

deep.surprise_reason: The numbers are classical (−1/12, 5/12). The motivic refinement with a 1/|Aut| weighting, and especially the explicit ζ_2, ζ_3 corrections over Spec Z, form an early and coherent unpublished computation of motivic orbifold classes of moduli stacks. It is notable as history but not a deep new result.
transcription_corrections: The '31' at the top is a page number, not part of the text.
In the second line of (79), the struck-out text should read just '= ½(T(1) − 1) + 5/12'; the inserted '+T(1)+' is a crossed-out fragment.
Under [M̂^∞_{1,1}] the handwriting has '‖ 1/2', i.e. [M̂^∞_{1,1}] = 1/2 as an annotation, not a separate line.
'une autre calcul' should read 'un autre calcul'.
S_1 refers to the curve with automorphism group Z/6Z; the struck-out text after S_1 is illegible.
In the next page's transcription, the coefficient '7/6' should be '1/6'.
